definition_zh: 不成功的；夭折的；中途失败的；发育不全的
definition_en: failing to achieve its purpose, or coming to an end before completion
core_image: 刚点火的火箭在半空断成两截，落回地面
scene: 队伍在山口折返，暴风雪让这次突袭彻底落空。 The abortive raid ended before the troops reached the pass.
sceneCN: 这里 abortive 是「中途失败的」（第 1 个义项：行动未达目的便告终止）；句意为这次突袭在部队抵达山口前就失败了。

pos.zh: 失败的；夭折的
（医学）顿挫的；（生物学）发育不全的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「中止；流产」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「流产；中止」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「失败地；中途终止地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「失败性；夭折状态」

senses.title: Failing to reach its aim
senses.definition: of an action or attempt, ending in failure before its goal is reached
senses.definitionCN: 指行动或尝试在达到目标之前以失败告终
senses.example: The rescue was an abortive attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 这次救援是一次失败的尝试。
senses.why: Latin aboriri meant 'to miscarry', from ab- 'away' and oriri 'to be born'; an abortive action is one whose outcome never comes to birth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aboriri 意为「流产」，由 ab-（离开）与 oriri（出生）构成；abortive 的行动就是结果从未「出生」的行动。

senses.title: Of a plan that collapses
senses.definition: of a plan or scheme, failing before it can be carried out
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或方案在付诸实施前就失败
senses.example: Their abortive plan cost the company a fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夭折的计划让公司损失了一大笔钱。
senses.why: A plan is expected to be 'born' in action; if it collapses early, it is abortive in the same obstetrical image.
senses.whyCN: 计划本应在行动中「诞生」；若早早崩解，就同样落入这个产科意象，成为 abortive。

senses.title: Of a revolt that fails
senses.definition: describing a uprising or coup that is put down or collapses
senses.definitionCN: 形容被镇压或自行瓦解的起义或政变
senses.example: The abortive uprising lasted only two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败的起义只持续了两天。
senses.why: A revolt is an attempted birth of a new order; crushed before it takes hold, it earns the word.
senses.whyCN: 起义是试图让新秩序「诞生」；在站稳之前被压碎，就得到这个词。

senses.title: Of medical treatment
senses.definition: describing treatment that stops a disease in its early stage
senses.definitionCN: 形容在疾病早期将其截断的治疗
senses.example: Doctors used abortive treatment to shorten the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用顿挫疗法缩短病程。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the 'cut short' sense literally: the treatment aborts the disease's course.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了字面的「截断」义：这种治疗把疾病的进程截断。

senses.title: Of an organ that never develops
senses.definition: of a body part, remaining small and non-functional
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位保持很小且无功能
senses.example: The whale retains an abortive hind limb.
senses.exampleCN: 鲸保留着一条发育不全的后肢。
senses.why: Biology borrows the image of a process that stops before completion: the organ's growth is aborted.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「过程未完成便停止」的意象：这个器官的生长被中止了。

senses.title: Of a pregnancy that ends early
senses.definition: describing a pregnancy or birth process that ends before it can continue
senses.definitionCN: 形容在继续之前就终止的妊娠或生产进程
senses.example: The term abortive is used for therapies that prevent a pregnancy from continuing.
senses.exampleCN: abortive 一词用于阻止妊娠继续的疗法。
senses.why: This is the literal source of the word: a process that should have led to birth stops on the way.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最字面的来源：本应导向出生的过程在中途停下。

senses.title: Of an effort that comes to nothing
senses.definition: of work or effort, producing no lasting result
senses.definitionCN: 指工作或努力没有产生持久结果
senses.example: All their abortive efforts left the bridge unbuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有徒劳的努力都没能让桥建成。
senses.why: Effort is expected to give birth to a result; when nothing is delivered, the effort is abortive.
senses.whyCN: 努力本应「生出」结果；当什么也没产出时，这份努力就是 abortive。

senses.title: Of a movement that stops short
senses.titleCN: 中途停止的运动或进程
senses.definition: of a process or movement, halting before its natural end
senses.definitionCN: 指进程或运动在自然结束前停下
senses.example: The reform was an abortive move that changed nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革是一次中途停止、什么也没改变的举动。
senses.why: The general sense is simply 'cut off before completion', the widest extension of the original image.
senses.whyCN: 最一般的义项就是「在完成前被截断」，这是原初意象最宽的延伸。

intro.en: Abortive comes from the Latin verb for miscarrying, whose parts mean 'away' and 'to be born'.
intro.cn: abortive 来自表示「流产」的拉丁语动词，其成分意为「离开」与「出生」。

items.en: oriri meant 'to rise, appear, be born'; it also produced origin and orient.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现、出生」，也衍生出 origin 与 orient。

items.en: ab is the preposition 'from, away from'.
items.cn: ab 是介词，意为「从、离开」。

items.en: aboriri meant 'to miscarry, fail to be born', built from ab- and oriri.
items.cn: aboriri 意为「流产、未能出生」，由 ab- 与 oriri 构成。

items.en: The past participle abortus gave the noun for a miscarriage and the adjective abortivus.
items.cn: 过去分词 abortus 构成表示流产的名词，并衍生出形容词 abortivus。

items.en: English adopted abortive first in the medical sense and then for any failed enterprise.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 abortive 的医学义，随后用于任何失败的事业。

items.en: Modern usage applies the word to plans, revolts, efforts, and underdeveloped organs.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词用于计划、起义、努力与发育不全的器官。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, noun, and adverb from the same family; the second gathers adjectives for failure and futility.
note.cn: 第一组收同族的动词、名词与副词；第二组收表示失败与徒劳的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stop a process before it finishes.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「中止、流产」，指在完成前停止某个过程。

entries.definition: The noun for the ending of a pregnancy or the failure of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流产；中止」，指妊娠终止或进程失败。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a failed or cut-short way'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「失败地、中途终止地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being abortive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失败性、夭折状态」。

entries.definition: Not achieving the intended result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不成功的」，未达到预期结果。

entries.definition: Useless because it cannot produce a result.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒劳的」，因无法产生结果而无用。

entries.definition: Producing no useful outcome, like a tree with no fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无成果的」，像不结果的树一样没有有用产出。

entries.definition: Having not succeeded in what was attempted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失败的」，在尝试的事情上没有成功。

entries.definition: Producing no result despite effort.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒然的」，尽管努力却没有结果。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the obstetrical image behind the word and the standard collocations; the abstract hooks picture a process cut off midway.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用词后的产科意象与标准搭配；抽象记忆点想象中途被截断的过程。

normal.en: Abortive and abort share the Latin image of a birth that does not happen.
normal.cn: abortive 与 abort 共享「未能出生的生产」这一拉丁意象。

normal.en: An abortive attempt, an abortive coup, and an abortive plan are standard collocations.
normal.cn: an abortive attempt、an abortive coup、an abortive plan 都是标准搭配。

normal.en: Abortive treatment is a medical phrase for stopping a disease early.
normal.cn: abortive treatment 是医学术语，指早期截断疾病。

normal.en: Abortive organ describes a body part that never fully develops.
normal.cn: abortive organ 指从未完全发育的身体部位。

normal.en: The -ive ending turns the action into a quality: what fails is abortive.
normal.cn: -ive 结尾把动作变成性质：失败的东西就是 abortive。

abstract.en: Picture a rocket that breaks apart in mid-air and falls back to the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象火箭在半空断成两截，落回发射台。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge half built, then abandoned with its arches open to the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一座建到一半就被放弃的桥，拱架空对天空。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that sprouts, then withers before the first leaf opens.
abstract.cn: 想象种子发了芽，却在第一片叶子展开前枯萎。

examples.en: The attack was abortive and the troops withdrew.
examples.cn: 进攻失败，部队撤退了。

examples.en: They made an abortive attempt to reach the summit.
examples.cn: 他们尝试登顶，但未能成功。

examples.en: The plan proved abortive from the start.
examples.cn: 这个计划从一开始就注定失败。

branches.cn: 起义或政变在站稳前被压碎。

definition_en: relating to words, especially words that are spoken rather than written
core_image: 一串声音从嘴里出来，在空中排成可数的词，再落进对方的耳朵
scene: 面试结束前，主考官提醒候选人把口头承诺写成邮件，他说： Please put your verbal promise in writing.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「口头说出的、以说话方式作出的」（第 1 个义项：以口头表达而非书面写下）；句意为主考官请候选人把口头承诺落实为书面文字。

senses.title: Spoken rather than written
senses.titleCN: 口头说出的，而非写下的
senses.definition: expressed in speech rather than in writing
senses.definitionCN: 以口头说出而不是以书面形式表达的
senses.example: She gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了口头警告，而没有发出书面警告。
senses.why: The root means 'word', and when a word is contrasted with a written document, the channel that remains is the voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根意为「词」；当它与书面文件相对时，剩下的渠道就是说话的声音。

senses.title: Relating to words or language
senses.definition: concerned with words and with the ability to use them
senses.definitionCN: 与词语以及运用词语的能力有关的
senses.example: Verbal ability predicts later reading success.
senses.exampleCN: 言语能力可以预测日后的阅读表现。
senses.why: The adjective was formed from the Latin noun for 'word', so its broadest job is simply to label anything that has to do with words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表示「词」的拉丁名词构成，因此最宽的用法就是给一切与词语有关的事物贴标签。

senses.title: Word-for-word and literal
senses.definition: following the exact words of an original rather than its overall meaning
senses.definitionCN: 照着原文的每一个词，而不是照着整体意思
senses.example: A verbal translation often misses the tone of the original.
senses.exampleCN: 逐字翻译常常丢掉原文的语气。
senses.why: If each word is handled separately, the translation becomes a row of separate words rather than one living sentence.
senses.whyCN: 若把每个词单独处理，译文就成了一排孤立的词，而不是一句活的话。

senses.title: Relating to a verb in grammar
senses.definition: relating to a verb or to a form built from a verb
senses.definitionCN: 与动词有关，或与由动词构成的形式有关
senses.example: The verbal ending changes with tense and person.
senses.exampleCN: 动词词尾随时态与人称变化。
senses.why: Latin used the same noun for 'word' and for 'verb', because the verb is the word that carries the action of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用同一个名词既指「词」也指「动词」，因为动词是承载句子动作的那个词。

senses.title: Using too many words
senses.definition: using more words than are needed to make a point
senses.definitionCN: 表达一个意思时用了超出需要的词
senses.example: His verbal style buried the main point under qualifications.
senses.exampleCN: 他冗长的说话方式把重点埋在一堆限定语下面。
senses.why: A person who piles up words is still working with words, but the abundance itself becomes the noticeable quality.
senses.whyCN: 堆词的人仍然在处理词语，只是词语的数量本身成了最显眼的特点。

senses.title: Words without matching action
senses.titleCN: 只有言辞而没有行动的
senses.definition: expressed in words but not supported by real action
senses.definitionCN: 只用言辞表达，却没有实际行动支撑
senses.example: The agreement was merely verbal and was never carried out.
senses.exampleCN: 那项约定只是口头上的，从未落实。
senses.why: When words are set against deeds, calling something verbal is a way of saying that only the talking half exists.
senses.whyCN: 当词语与行动相对时，说某事只是口头上的，就等于说只有说话那一半存在。

senses.title: Oral in a legal sense
senses.titleCN: 法律意义上的口头形式
senses.definition: made by speech rather than set down in a written instrument
senses.definitionCN: 以说话方式作出，而不是写在正式文书里
senses.example: A verbal contract can still bind the parties in some cases.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些情形下，口头合同仍能约束双方。
senses.why: Law separates a spoken declaration from a signed paper, and the word marks the side that leaves no written record.
senses.whyCN: 法律把口头声明与签字文件分开，这个词标记的正是没有留下书面记录的那一边。

senses.title: Carried by words, not by gestures
senses.titleCN: 以词语而非手势传递的
senses.definition: communicated through words rather than through bodily signals
senses.definitionCN: 通过词语而不是通过身体信号传递的
senses.example: The verbal message was clear, but the gestures softened it.
senses.exampleCN: 言语信息很清楚，但手势让它变得柔和。
senses.why: Communication research splits a message into the word channel and the body channel, and this sense names the word channel.
senses.whyCN: 交流研究把一次信息分成词语渠道与身体渠道，这个义项命名的正是词语渠道。

intro.en: Verbal comes through Middle French from Late Latin verbalis 'of words', built on Latin verbum 'word'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: verbal 经中古法语来自晚期拉丁语 verbalis「词的」，由拉丁语 verbum「词」加形容词后缀构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Verbum meant 'word' and was also the grammar term for 'verb'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link often suggested to an Indo-European root for speaking is a reconstruction, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: verbum 意为「词」，在语法中也指「动词」。其更深来源未得到证明；常有人把它系于某个表示「说话」的印欧词根，那只是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The adjective verbalis 'relating to words' was formed from verbum and passed into learned usage.
items.cn: 形容词 verbalis「与词有关的」由 verbum 构成，并进入学术用语。

items.en: Middle French verbal carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the broad sense 'of words'.
items.cn: 中古法语 verbal 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于「与词有关的」这一宽泛意义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word was regularly opposed to written, naming what is said aloud instead of what is set down on paper.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已常与「书面的」相对，指口头说出而非写在纸上的内容。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'of a verb' appears in the seventeenth century, and the noun for a verb-derived form developed later.
items.cn: 「与动词有关的」这一语法义在十七世纪出现，指动词性形式的名词义随后发展出来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of the spoken sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of verbum remains unsettled, so any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：口头义的确切首见年代没有定论，verbum 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to verbal but follow different roots or different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近、但词根或前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built on the same Latin word for 'word', but it means in exactly the same words, word for word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁语表示「词」的词，但意思是「逐字地、一字不差地」。

entries.definition: From a Latin adjective meaning 'full of words'; it describes speech or writing that uses far too many words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「充满词」的拉丁形容词，形容说话或写作用了过多词语。

entries.definition: It looks like a relative of the word root, but it comes from a Latin word for a home-born slave, later 'native'; it names the everyday language of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 外形像同族词，其实来自拉丁语指「家中出生的奴仆」、后转指「本地的」一词；它指一个地方日常使用的语言。

entries.definition: It descends from the same word stock through French and means an excess of words, often empty or official wording.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语同出这一词群，意思是词语过量，常指空洞或官样文字。

entries.definition: The standard adjective for what is spoken rather than written; it comes from a different Latin root meaning 'mouth'.
entries.definitionCN: 指口头而非书面的标准形容词；它来自另一个意为「嘴」的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The ordinary English participle for language produced by voice; it is plainer than verbal and lacks the grammatical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指用嗓音说出的语言的普通英语分词，比 verbal 朴素，也没有那些语法义。

entries.definition: Relating to language as a system; verbal can focus narrowly on individual words.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为系统的语言有关；verbal 可以只聚焦于一个个词。

entries.definition: A plain adjective for writing or speech that uses too many words, close to the fifth sense of verbal.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话或写作词句过多的朴素形容词，接近 verbal 的第 5 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real contrasts and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的对比与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'word', so verbal is the adjective for anything word-shaped.
normal.cn: 词根意为「词」，因此这个词就是给一切「词形状」的事物作形容词。

normal.en: The same root yields the adverb meaning word for word and the adjective meaning full of words.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成表示「逐字地」的副词与表示「满口是词」的形容词。

normal.en: Contrast pair: a verbal promise is spoken, while a written promise is on paper.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：口头的承诺用嘴说，书面的承诺落在纸上。

normal.en: Grammar note: a verbal noun is a noun built from a verb, such as a gerund.
normal.cn: 语法提示：动词性名词是由动词构成的名词，如动名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spoken sense: verbal agreement, verbal abuse, verbal skills.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「口头」义：口头协议、言语辱骂、语言能力。

abstract.en: Picture words as small stones a speaker hands over one by one.
abstract.cn: 把词语想成说话人一颗颗递过去的小石子。

abstract.en: Picture a signed page and a spoken sentence placed on two sides of a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签好的纸和一句说出的话被放在天平两端。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence made only of separate bricks, with no mortar between them.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话只用一块块独立的砖垒成，砖与砖之间没有灰浆。

examples.en: The manager gave only a verbal warning, so nothing appeared in the file.
examples.cn: 经理只做了口头警告，因此档案里没有留下任何记录。

examples.en: Her verbal skills made her a strong debater in seminars.
examples.cn: 她的言语能力使她在研讨会上成为强有力的辩手。

examples.en: A verbal translation of the poem lost its rhythm completely.
examples.cn: 这首诗的逐字翻译完全丢掉了节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「我播」：我播出去的是嘴上说的话 → 口头的、词语的

root: 拉丁语 verbum「词、动词」加关系形容词后缀构成晚期拉丁语 verbalis；verbum 更深来源不确定，把它系于某个表示「说话」的印欧词根仅为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all start from one idea, the word as a unit, and then divide by channel: spoken, written, grammatical, literal, excessive, unsupported by action, legal and bodily.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个起点出发，即「词」这个单位，然后按渠道分叉：口说、书写、语法、逐字、冗长、无行动支撑、法律形式与身体信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken word leaving the mouth as a small, countable object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个说出的词像可数的小物件一样离开嘴巴。

branches.en: SPOKEN CHANNEL: both the everyday warning and the legal declaration exist only in voice.
branches.cn: 口头渠道：日常警告与法律声明都只存在于声音里。

branches.en: WORD CARRIER: words themselves carry the message, whether against gestures or as a general ability.
branches.cn: 词语载体：无论与手势相对，还是作为一般能力，承载信息的都是词语本身。

branches.en: ONE WORD AT A TIME: literal translation treats each word as a separate unit.
branches.cn: 逐词处理：逐字翻译把每个词当作独立单位。

branches.en: VERB AND VERBOSITY: the same root names the action word and the habit of piling words up.
branches.cn: 动词与冗词：同一词根既命名动作词，也命名堆词的毛病。

branches.en: WORD WITHOUT DEED: the promise exists in speech but never becomes an act.
branches.cn: 有言无行：承诺只存在于言语中，从未变成行动。

intro.en: Verbal is built from a Latin root and a Latin adjectival suffix, and the same pieces recur across a small but active word family.
intro.cn: verbal 由一个拉丁词根与一个拉丁形容词后缀构成，同样的部件反复出现在一个小而活跃的词族里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbum 'word' supplies verbal, verbatim, verbose, proverb and verb; the suffix -alis marks the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「词」的词根衍生出表示「言语的」「逐字的」「啰嗦的」「谚语」「动词」的一组词；形容词后缀标记关系。

items.meaning: word; also the grammar term for verb
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名言语的最小单位。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: Verbal ability is tested in the first section.
items.exampleCN: 言语能力在第一部分接受测试。

items.example: She agreed verbally but never signed.
items.exampleCN: 她口头同意了，却始终没有签字。

items.example: He verbalized the feeling he had hidden for years.
items.exampleCN: 他把藏了多年的感受说了出来。

items.meaning: the act of putting something into words
items.meaningCN: 把某事变成词语的行为
items.example: Her verbalization of the plan made it easier to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她把计划说出来，使人更容易跟上。

items.example: He repeated the message verbatim.
items.exampleCN: 他一字不差地复述了那条信息。

items.example: The verbose report hid its conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 这份啰嗦的报告把结论藏了起来。

items.meaning: a saying passed down in fixed words
items.meaningCN: 以固定词句传下来的谚语
items.example: The old proverb still fits the case.
items.exampleCN: 那句老谚语仍适用于这件事。

definition_zh: 起义；暴动；（古义）起身、上升
definition_en: a spontaneous popular revolt, especially one that is short, local or sudden
core_image: 夜里一条窄巷挤满人，火把把墙照红，前排的人正把木箱推倒当台阶
scene: 监狱内院的铁门半开，走廊上散落着纸片与被推翻的桌椅。 The prison uprising ended when the guards opened the inner gate.
sceneCN: 这里 uprising 指「被统治者突然发起的反抗事件」（第 2 个义项：范围有限的暴动）；句意为狱警打开内门后，这场监狱暴动结束了。场景物件：铁门、散落的纸片、翻倒的桌椅、火把。

pos.zh: 起义；暴动；（古义）起身、上升

senses.title: An armed popular revolt
senses.definition: a rising of ordinary people against those who rule them, often with weapons
senses.definitionCN: 普通民众对统治者的起事，常持武器
senses.example: The uprising began in the market and reached the barracks by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 起义从市场开始，到中午已传到兵营。
senses.why: uprising is simply 'a rising up', and English applied the physical verb to crowds long before it became a political noun.
senses.whyCN: uprising 本只是「向上起身」，英语把这个身体动词用在人群上，远早于它成为政治名词。

senses.title: A sudden local riot
senses.definition: a short revolt inside one institution or district, such as a prison or camp
senses.definitionCN: 发生在单一机构或街区内的短暂反抗，如监狱或营地
senses.example: The prison uprising ended when the guards opened the inner gate.
senses.exampleCN: 狱警打开内门后，这场监狱暴动结束了。
senses.why: the word suits events measured in hours, which is why prisons, camps and ships supply so many examples.
senses.whyCN: 这个词适合以小时计的事件，因此监狱、营地与船只提供了大量用例。

senses.title: A named historical rising
senses.definition: a particular rising recorded under a name and a date
senses.definitionCN: 以名号与年代载入史册的某次起事
senses.example: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising is remembered for lasting a month.
senses.exampleCN: 华沙隔都起义因坚持一个月而被记住。
senses.why: historians make proper names out of events, and the compound keeps the plain noun inside the title.
senses.whyCN: 史家把事件变成专名，复合标题里仍保留这个朴素名词。

senses.title: A mass protest movement
senses.titleCN: 非暴力的群众抗争浪潮
senses.definition: a broad campaign of civil resistance that may avoid weapons altogether
senses.definitionCN: 可能完全不动武的广泛民间抵抗运动
senses.example: A quiet uprising of parents filled the council chamber week after week.
senses.exampleCN: 一场家长的静默抗争一周又一周地坐满议事厅。
senses.why: the metaphor no longer needs guns: any mass refusal that rises from below can take the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻不再需要枪：任何自下而上的大规模拒绝都能用这个名字。

senses.title: A national independence rising
senses.definition: a rising of a subject people seeking to end foreign rule
senses.definitionCN: 被统治民族为结束外来统治而发动的起事
senses.example: The national uprising of 1916 is taught in every school.
senses.exampleCN: 一九一六年的民族起义在每所学校都被讲授。
senses.why: when the unit is a people rather than a crowd, the word gains the weight of sovereignty.
senses.whyCN: 当单位是一个民族而非一群人之时，这个词便带上了主权分量。

senses.title: The literal act of rising
senses.definition: the physical act of getting up or of a thing moving upward, the oldest sense
senses.definitionCN: 起身或物体向上移动的实感动作，是最早的词义
senses.example: The prayer book still speaks of the uprising of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 祈祷书里仍说着太阳的升起。
senses.why: the political sense took over, yet poetry and liturgy kept the literal one alive.
senses.whyCN: 政治义占了上风，诗歌与礼仪却让实感义活了下来。

senses.title: A surge of feeling
senses.definition: a rising movement of emotion or force inside a person or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 人或人群中情绪或力量的涌动
senses.example: An uprising of anger carried the crowd past the barricade.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵愤怒的涌起把人群推过了街垒。
senses.why: the same upward motion is mapped onto feeling, so an emotion can rise like a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向上运动被映射到情绪上，情绪于是可以像人群一样升起。

senses.title: A collective outcry online
senses.definition: a rapid mass protest organised through social media rather than streets
senses.definitionCN: 借助社交媒体而非街头迅速组织的大规模抗议
senses.example: The hashtag turned a local complaint into a digital uprising overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那个话题标签一夜之间把一桩地方投诉变成一场网络声讨。
senses.why: new media gave the old word a new stage, and the rising now happens in feeds.
senses.whyCN: 新媒体给这个旧词一个新舞台，起身发生在信息流里。

intro.en: Uprising is a native English compound of up and rising, and its political sense is only a few centuries old.
intro.cn: uprising 是英语本族复合词，由 up 与 rising 构成，其政治义只有数百年历史。

items.en: Uprising joins the adverb up to rising, the verbal noun of rise, with no Latin element at all.
items.cn: uprising 把副词 up 接在 rise 的动名词 rising 上，完全不含拉丁成分。

items.en: Rise goes back to Old English rīsan 'to get up, rise', a Germanic verb with cognates in Dutch rijzen and Old High German rīsan.
items.cn: rise 上承古英语 rīsan「起身、上升」，是日耳曼动词，在荷兰语 rijzen 与古高地德语 rīsan 有同源词。

items.en: In the fourteenth century an uprising was simply the act of getting up or the rising of a heavenly body.
items.cn: 14 世纪时，uprising 只指起身的动作或天体的升起。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word was used for a popular rising against rulers, and this sense drove out the literal one.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，这个词被用于民众对统治者的起事，这一义逐渐挤走了实感义。

items.en: Today uprising usually names a short, local or spontaneous revolt, while longer organised ones are called rebellions or revolutions.
items.cn: 今天 uprising 多指短暂、局部或自发的起事，较长久的组织化起事则称 rebellion 或 revolution。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation for the revolt sense is dated loosely to the 1560s, and the literal sense lingered in poetry after that.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：起事义的最早书证只能约略定在 16 世纪六十年代；实感义此后仍在诗歌中延续。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built on the same rise family; group two holds the rival names for revolts.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 rise 词族的形近词；第二组是各类起事的竞争性名称。

entries.definition: The general noun of rising, which can also mean a revolt in older British usage, without the up-.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指上升的普通名词，旧英式用法也可指起事，只是没有 up-。

entries.definition: A rarer single-word form meaning to rise up; the longer uprising is the everyday noun.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的单词形式，意为升起；日常名词用较长的 uprising。

entries.definition: A surge of activity or feeling, from Latin surgere 'to rise', and never a political rising.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或情绪的骤增，出自拉丁 surgere「升起」，从不指政治起事。

entries.definition: A heavy disturbance or overturning, from heave, broader than a single rising.
entries.definitionCN: 指剧烈的动荡或翻覆，出自 heave，比单次起事更宽。

entries.definition: Stresses the casting off of allegiance, and can also mean to disgust.
entries.definitionCN: 强调抛弃效忠，也可指使人厌恶。

entries.definition: Implies leaders, plans and duration; an uprising is usually quicker and looser.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示领袖、计划与持续时间；uprising 通常更快、更松散。

entries.definition: The formal or legal name for a rising against the state, used in statutes and charges.
entries.definitionCN: 对国家起事的正式或法律名称，见于法规与控罪。

entries.definition: Crowd violence that may have no political aim; an uprising always has a target above it.
entries.definitionCN: 人群暴力，可能没有政治目标；uprising 总有上方的目标。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a native compound, a real Germanic verb and real historical titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：本族复合词、真实的日耳曼动词与真实历史标题。

normal.en: up + rising: the plainest possible description of a crowd getting to its feet.
normal.cn: up + rising：对人群站起来这件事最直白的描述。

normal.en: The rise family runs rise, rose, risen, rising, uprise, uprising.
normal.cn: rise 词族包括 rise、rose、risen、rising、uprise、uprising。

normal.en: No Latin here: the word is native English, unlike revolt or rebellion.
normal.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：与 revolt、rebellion 不同，它是英语本族词。

normal.en: Titles preserve it: the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, the Soweto Uprising.
normal.cn: 专名保留了它：华沙隔都起义、索韦托起义。

normal.en: Scale words pair with it: armed, popular, prison, national.
normal.cn: 表规模的词与它搭配：武装的、民众的、监狱的、民族的。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow lane packed with people and torches at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一条窄巷挤满人与火把。

abstract.en: Picture a crate pushed over to serve as a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只木箱被推倒，当作台阶。

abstract.en: Picture a hall where every hand goes up at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座大厅里所有手同时举起。

examples.en: The uprising spread from one district to four within a week.
examples.cn: 起义一周内从一区蔓延到四区。

examples.en: A prison uprising usually ends at the inner gate.
examples.cn: 监狱暴动通常止于内门。

examples.en: The history class compared the uprising with the later rebellion.
examples.cn: 历史课把这次起义与后来的叛乱作了比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普莱辛」听似「往上立身」——被压住的人一齐立起来 → 起义、暴动

root: 英语本族复合词：up「向上」+ rising（rise 的动名词）；rise 上承古英语 rīsan「起身、上升」，属日耳曼语族，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rise from a body to a crowd: the armed rising, the local riot, the named event, the non-violent campaign, the national struggle, the literal getting up, the surge of feeling and the online outcry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从身体升到人群：武装起事、局部暴动、有专名的事件、非暴力抗争、民族斗争、实感起身、情绪涌起与网络声讨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow lane packed with people and torches, a crate pushed over as a step.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条挤满人与火把的窄巷，一只木箱被推倒当台阶。

branches.en: PEOPLE IN ARMS: the general popular rising and the national struggle differ in scale, not in gesture.
branches.cn: 武装的民众：泛指民众起事与民族斗争差别在规模，不在姿势。

branches.en: SUDDEN AND LOCAL: a prison yard hosts a rising measured in hours rather than in months.
branches.cn: 突然与局部：监狱院子里的一场起事以小时而非月计。

branches.en: NAMED AND PEACEFUL: history turns one into a title, while civil resistance proves the word needs no weapons.
branches.cn: 专名与和平：历史把一次变成标题，民间抵抗则证明这个词不需要武器。

branches.en: BODY AND FEELING: the oldest sense is getting up, and emotion borrows the same upward motion.
branches.cn: 身体与情绪：最早的义项是起身，情绪借用同一种向上运动。

branches.en: NEW STAGE: the rising now happens in feeds as often as in streets.
branches.cn: 新舞台：起身如今在信息流里发生的次数不亚于街头。

intro.en: Uprising is built only from native English pieces, so its whole structure can be read without leaving the Germanic layer.
intro.cn: uprising 只由英语本族成分构成，因此整个结构不必离开日耳曼层就能读通。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative here: the word is a native compound of up and rising, and its older relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族词：它是 up 与 rising 的本族复合词，较古的同族形式属日耳曼语。

items.structure: Old English up, adverb of direction
items.example: The particle gives the whole word its upward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个小词给整词向上的方向。

items.example: The verb is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into an event noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成事件名词。

items.example: The uprising lasted one night.
items.exampleCN: 那场暴动只持续一夜。

items.example: The old verb now survives mostly in poetry.
items.exampleCN: 这个旧动词如今多存于诗歌。

items.meaning: an act of rising, a revolt
items.example: A rising in the north worried the council.
items.exampleCN: 北方的一场起事让议会不安。

items.example: The risen sun cleared the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 升起的太阳越过山脊。

items.meaning: one who rises, or a vertical piece
items.example: The stair riser was cut from oak.
items.exampleCN: 楼梯竖板是橡木做的。

definition_zh: 酸碱度；pH 值（氢离子活度以十为底的负对数）
definition_en: a number expressing the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, equal to the negative logarithm of its hydrogen ion activity
core_image: 一支细玻璃探头插进样杯，屏幕上的数字停在一个小数，旁边摆着一排比色纸
scene: 检测员把探头伸进溪水，屏幕停在一个小数，随后才把水样送回实验室。 A meter dipped into the stream reports the pH before the sample is sent to the lab.
sceneCN: 这里 pH 指表示溶液酸碱程度的数值（第 1 个义项：酸碱度这一读数值）；句意：伸入溪水的仪表在水样送检之前就报出了酸碱度。图中可辨识物件：玻璃探头、读数屏、样杯、比色纸。

pos.zh: 酸碱度；pH 值

derivatives.zh: 由 pH 与表示仪器的名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度计」
由 pH 与表示标度的名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度标度」
按同一构词法把氢换成氢氧根所得，义为「氢氧根指数」

senses.title: The reading itself
senses.definition: the number that reports how acid or basic a solution is
senses.definitionCN: 报告溶液酸碱程度的那个数字
senses.example: A meter dipped into the stream reports the pH before the sample is sent to the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 伸入溪水的仪表在水样送检之前就报出了酸碱度。
senses.why: The symbol is a shorthand label for a single number, so the most common sense is simply the value one reads or hears.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号是一个数字的简写标签，因此最常见的义项就是人们读到或听到的那个值。

senses.title: The negative logarithm of hydrogen activity
senses.definition: the formal definition: minus the base-ten logarithm of the hydrogen ion activity in a solution
senses.definitionCN: 正式定义：溶液中氢离子活度以十为底的对数取负
senses.example: Each unit of pH stands for a tenfold change in hydrogen ion activity.
senses.exampleCN: 每一个 pH 单位代表氢离子活度十倍的变化。
senses.why: Because the numbers span many powers of ten, a logarithmic scale was chosen, and the symbol encodes that power.
senses.whyCN: 由于数值跨越许多个十的幂，人们选用对数尺度，而这个符号正编码了那个幂。

senses.title: A property of a particular solution
senses.definition: the acid or basic character of a named liquid, as in the pH of milk or of rain
senses.definitionCN: 某种指定液体的酸碱性格，如牛奶或雨水的 pH
senses.example: The pH of the milk fell as the bacteria grew.
senses.exampleCN: 随着细菌繁殖，牛奶的酸碱度下降。
senses.why: The reading is always of something, so the symbol also names a property that a particular liquid possesses.
senses.whyCN: 读数总归是关于某物的，因此这个符号也命名某一具体液体所具有的属性。

senses.title: What an instrument displays
senses.definition: the figure shown by a meter or test strip, which stands for the solution's condition
senses.definitionCN: 由仪表或试纸显示的数字，代表溶液的状况
senses.example: The meter's pH drifted until the probe was recalibrated.
senses.exampleCN: 在探头重新校准之前，仪表的酸碱度读数一直漂移。
senses.why: In practice people meet the value through a device, so the symbol is used for the display as well as for the chemical fact.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中人们通过器件遇到这个值，因此该符号既指化学事实，也指显示结果。

senses.title: A position on a numbered scale
senses.definition: a place on the conventional scale that runs from strongly acid to strongly basic, with seven as neutral
senses.definitionCN: 在从强酸到强碱的惯用尺度上的位置，以七为中性
senses.example: The scale usually runs from zero to fourteen, though real solutions can fall outside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这一尺度通常从零到十四，但实际溶液也可能落在其外。
senses.why: Because the readings are ordered, the word also names the axis itself, and people speak of being low or high on it.
senses.whyCN: 由于读数是排序的，这个词也命名那条轴本身，人们会说在轴上偏低或偏高。

senses.title: The balance of a living body
senses.definition: the tightly controlled acid-base level of blood or other body fluid, kept within a narrow range
senses.definitionCN: 血液或其他体液中受严格控制、维持在窄范围内的酸碱水平
senses.example: Doctors watch the pH of the blood during long surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间手术中医生会监测血液的酸碱度。
senses.why: Physiology applies the reading to a body that must hold it steady, so the number becomes a vital sign.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个读数用在一个必须维持稳定的身体上，于是这个数字变成一项生命体征。

senses.title: The condition of soil or water
senses.definition: the acid-base level of soil, rain, a lake or the sea, which shapes what can live there
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、雨水、湖泊或海洋的酸碱水平，决定那里能生存什么
senses.example: Soil pH decides whether the blueberries will thrive.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤酸碱度决定蓝莓能否长好。
senses.why: Environmental science uses the symbol as a property of places, where it acts as a long-lasting setting.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这个符号当作地点的属性，在那里它起长期背景的作用。

senses.title: A quantity to be adjusted
senses.definition: a controlled parameter that operators raise or lower by adding acid or base
senses.definitionCN: 操作者通过加酸或加碱来升高或降低的受控参数
senses.example: The plant adjusts the pH of the waste stream before releasing it.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂在排放前调节废液的酸碱度。
senses.why: Once the value can be measured and changed, it becomes a dial in a process rather than a mere observation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个值可以被测量并改变，它就变成流程中的一个旋钮，而不只是观察对象。

intro.en: pH was coined in 1909 by the Danish chemist Søren Sørensen as a compact notation for hydrogen ion power. Its parts are German and Greek rather than Latin.
intro.cn: pH 由丹麦化学家瑟伦森于 1909 年造出，作为「氢离子幂」的紧凑记号；其部件来自德语与希腊语，而非拉丁语。

items.en: Hydrogen goes back to Greek hydor 'water' plus -genes 'born', a name given to the gas because burning it produced water.
items.cn: hydrogen 上溯到希腊语 hydor「水」加 -genes「产生」，这个名称给该气体，是因为它燃烧时生成水。

items.en: French chemists named the gas hydrogène at the end of the eighteenth century, and English adopted hydrogen soon after.
items.cn: 法国化学家在 18 世纪末把该气体命名为 hydrogène，英语随后采用 hydrogen。

items.en: Sørensen took p from the German word for 'power', so the first element of the symbol stands for the exponent rather than for a quantity itself.
items.cn: 瑟伦森取德语中表示「幂」的词首字母，因此符号的第一个成分代表指数，而不是某个量本身。

items.en: Working on the acidity of solutions, Sørensen introduced the notation for the negative logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration, and the compact symbol spread at once.
items.cn: 瑟伦森在研究溶液的酸度时，为氢离子浓度的负对数引入这一记号，这个紧凑符号迅速传开。

items.en: Medicine, agriculture, water treatment and industry adopted the symbol in the following decades, each adding its own standard range.
items.cn: 医学、农业、水处理与工业在此后数十年采用该符号，各自加上自己的标准范围。

items.en: Source uncertain for one detail: the exact reasoning behind the letter p has been explained in more than one way; the German Potenz 'power' account is the most widely accepted, while Latin pondus 'weight' and French puissance have also been proposed, so no single reading is settled.
items.cn: 有一处细节来源不确定：字母 p 的确切由来曾有不止一种解释；德语 Potenz「幂」之说最为流行，也有人提出拉丁语 pondus「重量」与法语 puissance，因此并无单一结论被视为定论。

note.en: The first group is built with the same symbol pattern or names the instruments; the second group holds the quantities the symbol reports.
note.cn: 第一组用同一符号模式构成，或命名相关仪器；第二组是该符号所报告的各个量。

entries.definition: The same construction applied to hydroxide ion activity; it reports the basic side of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 对氢氧根离子活度施用同一构词法；它报告同一尺度的碱性一侧。

entries.definition: The device that reads the value; the symbol is a modifier inside the name of the tool.
entries.definitionCN: 读取该值的装置；符号是工具名称里的修饰成分。

entries.definition: The ordered range of readings; the symbol names the quantity, the compound names the ruler it sits on.
entries.definitionCN: 读数的有序范围；符号命名量，复合词命名它所依附的标尺。

entries.definition: A paper treated with dyes that change colour at different values; it displays the reading without electronics.
entries.definitionCN: 浸过染料、在不同数值下变色的纸；不用电子器件就能显示读数。

entries.definition: The measured degree of being acid; pH is one standard way of reporting that degree.
entries.definitionCN: 所测的呈酸程度；pH 是报告该程度的一种标准方式。

entries.definition: The degree of being basic, or water's capacity to absorb acid; related to pH but not the same measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 呈碱的程度，或水抵偿酸的能力；与 pH 相关，但不是同一种测量。

entries.definition: The amount of free hydrogen ions per volume; pH is its negative logarithm, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 单位体积内自由氢离子的量；pH 是该量的负对数，而不是量本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The p stands for the German word for power, and the H stands for hydrogen.
normal.cn: 字母 p 代表德语中表示「幂」的词，字母 H 代表氢。

normal.en: Every unit is a tenfold change in hydrogen ion activity, which is why the scale is logarithmic.
normal.cn: 每一个单位都是氢离子活度的十倍变化，这就是尺度取对数的原因。

normal.en: Fixed compounds mark the tools: pH meter, pH scale, pH paper.
normal.cn: 固定复合词标出工具：酸碱度计、酸碱度标度、酸碱度试纸。

normal.en: The neutral point is seven, and both directions run away from it.
normal.cn: 中性点是七，两个方向都从中性点向外延伸。

normal.en: Sørensen introduced the notation in 1909 while studying solution acidity.
normal.cn: 瑟伦森在 1909 年研究溶液酸度时引入了这一记号。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks get ten times farther apart at every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，每走一格，刻度间距就变成十倍。

abstract.en: Picture a single drop of colour spreading through a whole glass of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴颜色在一整杯水里慢慢散开。

abstract.en: Picture a dial in a plant room that someone turns until the needle sits in the green band.
abstract.cn: 想象厂房里一个表盘，有人转动它，直到指针落在绿色区段。

examples.en: Rain in the region often has a pH below five.
examples.cn: 该地区的雨水酸碱度常低于五。

examples.en: The technician calibrated the pH meter before sampling.
examples.cn: 技术员在取样前校准了酸碱度计。

examples.en: Buffers keep the pH steady when acid is added.
examples.cn: 加入酸时，缓冲体系使酸碱度保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「p（幂）+ H（氢）」——氢离子幂的缩写，就是酸碱度

root: 1909 年瑟伦森所造的记号：p 取自德语中表示「幂」的词，H 代表氢；氢一词出自希腊语 hydor「水」+ -genes「产生」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one logarithmic reading: the number itself, its formal definition, a property of a liquid, an instrument display, a position on the scale, a body's balance, a landscape's condition, and a parameter to adjust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个对数读数：数字本身、其正式定义、某液体的属性、仪器显示、尺度上的位置、身体的平衡、景观的状况，以及可调节的参数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a probe in a cup, a decimal frozen on the screen, and a row of colour strips beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：探头插在杯里，屏幕上停着一个小数，旁边摆着一排比色纸。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND ITS OWNER: the reading, and the particular liquid whose condition it reports.
branches.cn: 数字及其所属：读数，以及它所报告状况的那种液体。

branches.en: THE LOGARITHM: behind the number lies a power of ten, which is what makes the scale compress huge ranges.
branches.cn: 对数：数字背后是一个十的幂，正是它让尺度压缩了巨大的范围。

branches.en: THE DISPLAY: in daily work the value arrives through a device, so the symbol stands for what the screen shows.
branches.cn: 显示：在日常工作里，这个值通过器件抵达，于是符号代指屏幕所示。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND THE PLACE: the ordered scale, and the condition of a field, a lake or a sea upon it.
branches.cn: 轴与位置：有序的尺度，以及田、湖或海在这条轴上的状况。

branches.en: THE LIVING AND THE CONTROLLED: a body holds the number within a narrow band, while a plant turns it like a dial.
branches.cn: 生命与受控：身体把数字守在窄带内，而工厂把它当作旋钮来转。

intro.en: pH is a two-letter notation rather than a word with affixes, and each letter stands for a different source.
intro.cn: pH 不是带词缀的单词，而是一个两字母记号，每个字母各自代表不同的来源。

latinIntro.en: Latin plays no part in this symbol: the first element is German and the second goes back through French to Greek, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语在这个符号里没有角色：第一个成分来自德语，第二个经法语上溯希腊语，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.example: The notation fits on a dial or a label.
items.exampleCN: 这个记号可以印在表盘或标签上。

items.structure: abbreviation of the German word for power
items.example: The letter marks the exponent, not the amount.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母标的是指数，而非数量。

items.example: The second letter names the ion being counted.
items.exampleCN: 第二个字母命名被计数的离子。

items.structure: French hydrogène, from Greek words for water and born
items.meaning: the gas that makes water when burned
items.meaningCN: 燃烧时生成水的那种气体
items.example: Hydrogen was named for the water it produces.
items.exampleCN: 氢因其生成的水而得名。

items.example: The reading tracks the activity of the hydron.
items.exampleCN: 这个读数追踪裸氢离子的活度。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for a graduated range
items.example: Seven sits at the middle of the pH scale.
items.exampleCN: 七位于酸碱度标度的中间。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for an instrument
items.meaning: a device that reads the value
items.example: The pH meter needs calibration each morning.
items.exampleCN: 酸碱度计每天早上都要校准。

items.structure: the notation plus the word for a strip
items.example: The pH paper turned green in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 试纸在样品里变成了绿色。

derivatives.zh: 由 pH 与仪器名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度计」
由 pH 与标度名词复合而成，义为「酸碱度标度」
按同一构词法把氢换成氢氧根所得，义为「氢氧根指数」

definition_zh: 虚拟化；把物理资源抽象成多个独立虚拟环境的技术；服务器、桌面、网络或存储资源的虚拟化
definition_en: the creation of a virtual version of a resource, such as a server, desktop, network or storage system, so that it can be used independently of its physical form
core_image: 一台机柜里的服务器被划分成几个互不相见的隔间，每个隔间都以为自己独占整台机器
scene: 机房管理员把一台物理服务器的资源切成几个互不干扰的运行空间，各自装系统。 Virtualization lets one machine host several isolated systems.
sceneCN: 这里指把物理资源抽象成多个独立虚拟环境（第 2 个义项：服务器虚拟化）；句意为虚拟化让一台机器承载多个隔离的系统。图中可辨识物件：机柜、服务器、分隔框、指示灯。

pos.zh: 虚拟化；资源抽象；虚拟环境技术

derivatives.zh: 虚拟化工具；虚拟化实施者

senses.title: Making one resource look like many
senses.titleCN: 把一份资源看成许多份
senses.definition: the general act of abstracting a physical resource so that users see logical resources instead
senses.definitionCN: 把物理资源抽象化、使用户看到逻辑资源的一般做法
senses.example: Virtualization hides the number of disks behind one pool.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟化把磁盘数量藏在一个存储池后面。
senses.why: The verb virtualize plus -ation names the act of turning something real into something effective in software.
senses.whyCN: 动词「使虚拟化」加名词后缀「过程」，命名的是把真实之物变成软件中有效之物的动作。

senses.title: Splitting a server
senses.definition: the use of a hypervisor to run several separate operating systems on one physical server
senses.definitionCN: 用虚拟机监控程序在一台物理服务器上运行多个相互独立的操作系统
senses.example: Server virtualization cut the number of racks by half.
senses.exampleCN: 服务器虚拟化把机柜数量减少了一半。
senses.why: One machine can supply the effect of many, which is exactly the old 'effective, not physical' idea.
senses.whyCN: 一台机器能提供许多台的效果，这正是古老的「有效而非实体」那个念头。

senses.title: Desktop virtualization
senses.definition: the running of a user's desktop on a remote server and its delivery to a local screen
senses.definitionCN: 用户在远程服务器上运行桌面，再把画面送到本地屏幕
senses.example: Desktop virtualization lets staff log in from any machine.
senses.exampleCN: 桌面虚拟化让员工从任何一台机器登录。
senses.why: The desk itself becomes a software construct, so the workplace travels instead of the computer.
senses.whyCN: 办公桌本身成了软件构造，于是流动的是工作场所，而不是电脑。

senses.title: Network virtualization
senses.definition: the creation of several logical networks on top of shared physical links and switches
senses.definitionCN: 在共享的物理链路与交换机之上建立多个逻辑网络
senses.example: Network virtualization creates separate paths on one switch.
senses.exampleCN: 网络虚拟化在一台交换机上分出彼此独立的路径。
senses.why: Links that once belonged to one cable can now be divided by software, like lanes painted on a road.
senses.whyCN: 原本属于一根线缆的链路，如今可由软件划分，就像在一条路上画出车道。

senses.title: Storage virtualization
senses.definition: the pooling of separate physical storage devices into one logical store that can be managed as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 把分散的物理存储设备汇成一个可按整体管理的逻辑存储
senses.example: Storage virtualization merged four arrays into one pool.
senses.exampleCN: 存储虚拟化把四组阵列并成一个存储池。
senses.why: Many boxes become one box on the screen, which is the same abstraction applied to capacity.
senses.whyCN: 许多盒子在屏幕上变成一个盒子，这是同一套抽象用在容量上。

senses.title: Operating-system-level virtualization
senses.definition: the isolation of applications in containers that share one kernel instead of each carrying a full system
senses.definitionCN: 让应用在共享同一内核的容器中彼此隔离，而不必各自携带完整系统
senses.example: OS-level virtualization starts a container in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 操作系统级虚拟化在几秒内启动一个容器。
senses.why: Instead of faking whole machines, this branch fakes only the boundaries around a process.
senses.whyCN: 这一支不再伪造整台机器，只伪造进程周围的边界。

senses.title: Application virtualization
senses.definition: the delivery of an application in an isolated package so that it runs without a normal installation
senses.definitionCN: 把应用打包隔离后交付，使其无需常规安装即可运行
senses.example: Application virtualization runs the old program without installing it.
senses.exampleCN: 应用虚拟化让旧程序无需安装就能运行。
senses.why: The smallest thing that can be made virtual is a single program, and the word reaches its narrowest point.
senses.whyCN: 能被虚拟化的最小对象是单个程序，这个词也走到最窄处。

senses.title: Resource abstraction as a principle
senses.definition: the general computing principle of separating logical resources from the hardware that provides them
senses.definitionCN: 把逻辑资源与提供它们的硬件分开的一般计算原则
senses.example: Virtualization is the first step in building a private cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 虚拟化是搭建私有云的第一步。
senses.why: Once abstraction is named as a principle, it becomes the foundation of cloud and container systems.
senses.whyCN: 当抽象被命名为一项原则，它就成了云与容器系统的基础。

intro.en: Virtualization is virtual plus the verb suffix -ize and the noun suffix -ation. Virtual goes back to Late Latin virtualis 'having power', from virtus. The computing sense developed in the 1960s and spread with x86 virtual machines in the 2000s.
intro.cn: virtualization 由 virtual 加动词后缀 -ize 与名词后缀 -ation 构成。virtual 上溯晚期拉丁 virtualis「有力量的」，源自 virtus。计算义在二十世纪六十年代形成，并随二十一世纪的 x86 虚拟机普及。

items.en: Virtualis meant having power or producing an effect, and English virtual kept that sense of effectiveness without a separate form.
items.cn: virtualis 指有力量或能产生效果，英语 virtual 保留了这种「有效而无独立形态」的意思。

items.en: The verb suffix -ize, from Greek through Latin, turns an adjective into a verb meaning to make or to render.
items.cn: 动词后缀 -ize 经拉丁语来自希腊语，把形容词变成「使成为」的动词。

items.en: The noun suffix -ation, from Latin -atio, names the process or the result of that verb.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ation 来自拉丁 -atio，命名该动词的过程或结果。

items.en: IBM's CP-67 system in the late 1960s ran several virtual machines on one mainframe and established the term in computing.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代末，万国商业机器的 CP-67 系统在一台大型机上运行多台虚拟机，使该词在计算领域立住。

items.en: Virtualization of ordinary server hardware spread after VMware's 1999 release, when many small systems could share one physical machine.
items.cn: 普通服务器硬件的虚拟化在 VMware 一九九九年发布后普及，许多小系统得以共用一台物理机。

items.en: From the 2000s, operating-system-level containers added a lighter branch, so virtualization now covers machines, desktops, networks, storage and processes.
items.cn: 二十一世纪起，操作系统级容器增加了更轻的一支，虚拟化由此覆盖机器、桌面、网络、存储与进程。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like virtualization; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「virtualization」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what exists in effect or in software rather than as a separate object.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以效果或软件形式存在、而非独立实物的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to turn a physical resource into a logical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指把物理资源变成逻辑资源的动词。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective for resources already turned into software form.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，指已转成软件形态的资源。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning almost or in effect; it is not the adverb of this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「几乎、实际上」的副词，并不是这个名词的副词。

entries.definition: The state of being virtual, used in philosophy and media studies.
entries.definitionCN: 虚拟状态，用于哲学与媒介研究。

entries.definition: The act of removing detail so that a simpler logical view remains.
entries.definitionCN: 去除细节、留下更简单逻辑视图的做法。

entries.definition: Imitation of one system by another so that the same software can run.
entries.definitionCN: 用一个系统模仿另一个，使同样的软件得以运行。

entries.definition: Dividing a resource into separate parts, often without a full virtual machine.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分成若干独立部分，通常不涉及完整虚拟机。

entries.definition: Packaging an application with its dependencies so it runs isolated on a shared kernel.
entries.definitionCN: 把应用与依赖打包，使其在共享内核上隔离运行。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffixes, the real computing history and real product phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实后缀、真实计算史与真实产品搭配。

normal.en: The verb virtualize plus -ation simply names the process of making something virtual.
normal.cn: 动词 virtualize 加 -ation，直接命名「使某物虚拟化」的过程。

normal.en: The family runs virtual, virtualize, virtualized, virtualization and virtuality.
normal.cn: 同族词有 virtual、virtualize、virtualized、virtualization 与 virtuality。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: server, desktop, network, storage and application virtualization.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各支：服务器、桌面、网络、存储与应用虚拟化。

normal.en: A hypervisor is the program that runs several virtual machines on one host.
normal.cn: 虚拟机监控程序是在一台宿主上运行多台虚拟机的程序。

normal.en: Containers share one kernel, which makes them lighter than full virtual machines.
normal.cn: 容器共享一个内核，因此比完整虚拟机更轻。

abstract.en: Virtualization is many rooms drawn inside one building.
abstract.cn: 虚拟化是在一栋楼里画出许多房间。

abstract.en: Each room believes it has the whole building, and none of them can see the walls of the others.
abstract.cn: 每个房间都以为自己拥有整栋楼，却看不见别的房间的墙。

abstract.en: The abstraction is a promise: the logical view holds even when the hardware changes.
abstract.cn: 抽象是一句承诺：即使硬件更换，逻辑视图仍然成立。

examples.en: Virtualization let the lab retire six old servers without losing a single service.
examples.cn: 虚拟化让实验室退役了六台旧服务器却没有丢失任何一项服务。

examples.en: The course explains virtualization before it introduces cloud platforms.
examples.cn: 这门课在介绍云平台之前先讲虚拟化。

examples.en: Storage virtualization made the four arrays look like one large disk.
examples.cn: 存储虚拟化让四组阵列看起来像一块大磁盘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「虚拟 + 化」——把真的切成假的，每块都以为自己是全部：虚拟化

root: virtual 来自晚期拉丁 virtualis「有力量的」，加 -ize（使成为）与 -ation（过程）构成。计算义自二十世纪六十年代的大型机虚拟机开始，x86 虚拟化在九十年代末普及，容器又添一支。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one abstraction: a resource made logical, a server split, a desktop delivered, a network divided, storage pooled, a kernel shared, an application packaged, and the principle itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次抽象：资源被逻辑化、服务器被切开、桌面被送远、网络被划分、存储被汇集、内核被共享、应用被打包，最后是原则本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one server divided into sealed compartments, each believing it owns the whole machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台服务器被切成若干密封隔间，每个都以为自己独占整台机器。

branches.en: THE GENERAL ACT: a physical thing is replaced by a logical view that behaves the same.
branches.cn: 一般动作：物理之物被一个行为相同的逻辑视图取代。

branches.en: THE SPLIT SERVER: one machine hosts several systems that never meet.
branches.cn: 被切开的服务器：一台机器承载多个永不相见的系统。

branches.en: THE DISTANT DESK: the desktop lives on a server and appears on any screen.
branches.cn: 远方的桌面：桌面住在服务器上，却出现在任何屏幕上。

branches.en: THE DIVIDED AND POOLED RESOURCES: links are split into logical paths, disks are merged into one pool.
branches.cn: 被划分与被汇集的资源：链路分成逻辑路径，磁盘并成一个池。

branches.en: THE LIGHT BRANCHES: containers share a kernel, single applications are packaged, and abstraction becomes a principle.
branches.cn: 更轻的分支：容器共享内核，单个应用被打包，抽象上升为原则。

intro.en: Virtualization is virtual plus -ize plus -ation, built on Late Latin virtualis.
intro.cn: virtualization 是 virtual 加 -ize 再加 -ation，建立在晚期拉丁 virtualis 上。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin virtualis gives English virtual; English adds the Greek-Latin verb suffix -ize and the Latin noun suffix -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁 virtualis 衍生英语 virtual；英语再加希腊—拉丁动词后缀 -ize 与拉丁名词后缀 -ation。

items.exampleCN: 整个词族背后的形容词。

items.example: English extended it into computing.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到计算。

items.example: The verb names the change.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名变化。

items.example: The noun names the process.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名过程。

items.example: The participle describes the result.
items.exampleCN: 分词描述结果。

items.meaning: a tool or person that virtualizes
items.example: The agent suffix names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀点名执行者。

items.meaningCN: 表示「使成为」的动词后缀
items.example: It builds virtualize and modernize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virtualize 与 modernize 等词。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It builds virtualization and organization.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 virtualization 与 organization 等词。

items.meaning: a monitor that runs virtual machines
items.meaningCN: 运行虚拟机的监控程序
items.example: The word names the tool that performs this work.
items.exampleCN: 该词命名执行这项工作的工具。

definition_zh: 科学定律；对自然现象中稳定关系的简洁陈述
definition_en: a concise statement, supported by repeated evidence, that describes a regular relationship in nature
core_image: 墙上挂着一块只写一条简洁等式的牌子，旁边贴满历年核对无误的数据表
scene: 物理教室的墙上挂着一块牌子，只写一条简洁的等式，旁边贴满历年核对过的数据。 A scientific law describes what always happens under stated conditions, not why it happens.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：经反复验证、描述自然中稳定关系的陈述；句意为科学定律说明在给定条件下总会发生什么，而不解释为何发生。图中可辨识物件：等式牌、数据表、图钉、坐标轴。

pos.zh: 科学定律；自然规律（可数）

collocations.zh: 违反科学定律（多作修辞）

collocations.phrase: a scientific law and a theory
collocations.zh: 科学定律与理论（常作对比）

senses.title: A statement of regularity
senses.definition: a concise statement that a certain relationship holds whenever the stated conditions are met
senses.definitionCN: 一条简洁陈述：只要满足所述条件，某种关系就成立
senses.example: A scientific law describes what always happens under stated conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 科学定律说明在给定条件下总会发生什么。
senses.why: The word law was borrowed from legal language for something laid down; here what is laid down is a regularity, not a command.
senses.whyCN: 「定律」一词借自法律语言，本指被立下的东西；在这里被立下的是一条稳定关系，而不是命令。

senses.title: A named law of physics
senses.definition: one of the named statements, such as Newton's laws of motion, that organise a branch of physics
senses.definitionCN: 组织某一物理分支的具名陈述，如牛顿运动定律
senses.example: Newton's scientific laws still hold for ordinary speeds.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿的科学定律在寻常速度下依然成立。
senses.why: A name lets a whole pattern be cited in a sentence, which is why laws are named after their formulators.
senses.whyCN: 有了专名，一整套模式就能在一句话里被引用，因此定律常以提出者命名。

senses.title: The describing half of a pair
senses.definition: the part of knowledge that says what happens, as contrasted with a theory that says why
senses.definitionCN: 知识中说明「发生什么」的部分，与说明「为何发生」的理论相对
senses.example: A scientific law and a theory do different jobs and do not compete.
senses.exampleCN: 科学定律与理论各司其职，并不互相竞争。
senses.why: A statement of pattern and a statement of mechanism answer different questions, so the pair is not a ladder from weaker to stronger.
senses.whyCN: 对模式的陈述与对机制的陈述回答不同问题，因此这一对并不是由弱到强的阶梯。

senses.title: A quantitative empirical law
senses.definition: a law stating a measurable relation, often expressed as an equation, derived from experiment
senses.definitionCN: 陈述可测关系的定律，常写成等式，由实验得出
senses.example: Boyle's scientific law relates pressure and volume at fixed temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 玻意耳的科学定律描述定温下压强与体积的关系。
senses.why: Once a relation can be written as an equation, each new measurement can test it, and the law becomes a working tool.
senses.whyCN: 关系一旦能写成等式，每次新测量都能检验它，定律于是成为可用的工具。

senses.title: A law of conservation
senses.definition: a law stating that some quantity stays constant in a closed process, such as energy or momentum
senses.definitionCN: 陈述在封闭过程中某量保持不变的定律，如能量或动量
senses.example: The scientific law of conservation of energy survived every test.
senses.exampleCN: 能量守恒这条科学定律经受住了每一次检验。
senses.why: A conserved quantity is the strongest kind of regularity, because it says what cannot change rather than what usually does.
senses.whyCN: 守恒量是最强的一类稳定性，因为它说的是什么不能变，而不是通常怎样变。

senses.title: A law of nature, philosophically
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的自然规律
senses.definition: the idea that nature follows regularities that inquiry can discover, apart from any legislator
senses.definitionCN: 认为自然遵循可由探究发现的规律、且无需立法者的观念
senses.example: A scientific law of nature once implied a lawgiver, and the metaphor still troubles philosophers.
senses.exampleCN: 「自然规律」一说曾暗含立法者，这个比喻至今仍困扰哲学。
senses.why: The legal metaphor carried over: regularities were imagined as commands written into matter, and the image has never fully worn off.
senses.whyCN: 法律的比喻被继承了：稳定性被想象成写进物质的命令，这个意象从未完全褪去。

senses.title: A law in biology
senses.definition: a broad regularity in living systems, such as the patterns of inheritance, usually looser than a physical law
senses.definitionCN: 生命系统中的宽泛稳定性，如遗传模式，通常比物理定律宽松
senses.example: Mendel's scientific laws predict ratios rather than exact values.
senses.exampleCN: 孟德尔的科学定律预测比例，而非精确数值。
senses.why: Living systems carry variation, so biological laws tend to describe distributions, which is a weaker claim than a fixed equation.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统带有变异，因此生物定律多描述分布，这比固定等式是更弱的主张。

senses.title: A tendency in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的趋势陈述
senses.definition: an observed regularity in human affairs, stated as a tendency rather than an invariable rule
senses.definitionCN: 对人类事务中观察到的稳定性所作的陈述，多表述为趋势而非不变规则
senses.example: Economists speak of scientific laws of supply, though the regularities can break.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家谈供给的科学定律，尽管这些稳定性会失效。
senses.why: Human behaviour changes when people learn the prediction, so social regularities are stated as tendencies and hedged accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 人一旦知道预测就会改变行为，因此社会稳定性被表述为趋势，并相应加上限定。

senses.title: A mathematical law
senses.definition: a named theorem-like regularity, such as the law of large numbers, proved from stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 有专名、近似定理的稳定性，如大数定律，由所述前提证明
senses.example: The scientific law of large numbers steadies averages as samples grow.
senses.exampleCN: 大数这条科学定律使平均值随样本增大而稳定。
senses.why: Mathematics supplies regularities that need no experiment, and the word law is borrowed for them by analogy.
senses.whyCN: 数学提供无需实验的稳定性，人们便按类比把定律一词借了过去。

intro.en: Scientific law pairs a Latin-derived adjective with an Old Norse-derived noun. Science comes from scire 'to know'; law comes from Old Norse lag, 'something laid down', and has nothing to do with Latin lex.
intro.cn: scientific law 把拉丁语来源的形容词与古诺尔斯语来源的名词配在一起。science 出自 scire「知道」；law 出自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，与拉丁语 lex 无关。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge, and scientific is the adjective built on it in modern English.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识，scientific 是 modern English 在它上面构成的形容词。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down or set in place, and the plural lagu named the body of things laid down as custom.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下、被安置的东西，复数 lagu 指作为惯例立下的整套规定。

items.en: Old English borrowed lagu from Norse, and law kept the image of something laid down by authority.
items.cn: 古英语从诺尔斯语借入 lagu，law 保留了「由权威立下之物」的意象。

items.en: Latin lex and its stem leg- give legal, legislate and legitimate; those words are cousins in meaning, not sources of law.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex 及其词干 leg- 产生 legal、legislate 与 legitimate；这些词只是意思上的近亲，并非 law 的来源。

items.en: Writers on the new physics spoke of laws of nature, borrowing the legal metaphor for regularities found in matter.
items.cn: 新物理学的作者谈「自然规律」，把法律比喻借来描述物质中的稳定性。

items.en: The full phrase settled in the nineteenth century, and the modern contrast between law and theory was fixed in textbooks of the twentieth.
items.cn: 完整说法在十九世纪定型，现代「定律与理论」的对比则在二十世纪教科书中固定下来。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names neighbouring concepts in method.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个词中的一个；第二组是方法上的相邻概念。

entries.definition: A rule laid down by authority, or a regularity in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威立下的规则，或自然中的稳定关系。

entries.definition: Allowed by law; it belongs to the legal side, not the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 法律所允许的；属于法律一侧，而非科学一侧。

entries.definition: Following tested method; the adjective half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循检验方法的；短语中的形容词一半。

entries.definition: The organized knowledge behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的系统知识。

entries.definition: From Latin lex; it looks like a relative of law but comes down another line.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁语 lex；看似与「法律」同族，其实来自另一条线。

entries.definition: Lawful or genuine, from the same Latin legal stem as legal.
entries.definitionCN: 合法或正当的，与「合法的」一词同出拉丁法律词干。

entries.definition: An explanation of why something happens, the partner and not the rival of a law.
entries.definitionCN: 解释事情为何发生的体系，是定律的搭档而非对手。

entries.definition: A general rule that guides reasoning, often broader and less quantitative.
entries.definitionCN: 引导推理的一般规则，通常更宽泛、更少定量。

entries.definition: A testable guess that has not yet earned the name of law.
entries.definitionCN: 尚不足以称为定律的可检验猜测。

entries.definition: A stated regularity or instruction, wider in everyday use than law.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述的稳定性或指示，日常用法比定律更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real origins, the legal metaphor and the standard law-theory contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实来源、法律比喻，以及标准的定律与理论对比。

normal.en: Law came from Norse for something laid down, and a regularity laid down in matter is a law of nature.
normal.cn: law 来自诺尔斯语，指被放下之物；物质中被放下的稳定性就是自然规律。

normal.en: Scientific law is not from Latin lex; legal and legitimate come from that other line.
normal.cn: scientific law 并非出自拉丁语 lex；legal 与 legitimate 才来自那条线。

normal.en: A law says what happens; a theory says why. They answer different questions.
normal.cn: 定律说发生什么，理论说为何发生；两者回答不同问题。

normal.en: Boyle's law, Newton's laws and the conservation of energy are all named regularities.
normal.cn: 玻意耳定律、牛顿定律与能量守恒，都是有专名的稳定性。

normal.en: Biological laws predict ratios, because living systems carry variation.
normal.cn: 生物定律预测比例，因为生命系统带有变异。

abstract.en: A law is a promise nature has kept every time we looked, not a promise it has signed.
abstract.cn: 定律是自然在我们每次观察时都守住的承诺，不是它签署的契约。

abstract.en: The strongest law is the one that forbids something, like a quantity that cannot be lost.
abstract.cn: 最强的定律是禁止某事的定律，比如某个量不能消失。

abstract.en: Calling a regularity a law is a metaphor borrowed from courts, and the metaphor still asks who legislates.
abstract.cn: 把稳定性称作定律是从法庭借来的比喻，而这个比喻仍在追问谁在立法。

examples.en: A scientific law can be stated in one line and tested for centuries.
examples.cn: 一条科学定律能用一行写出，并被检验数百年。

examples.en: The students confused a scientific law with a theory and had to separate them.
examples.cn: 学生们把科学定律与理论混为一谈，后来不得不把它们分开。

examples.en: No scientific law forbids the pattern; it simply has never been seen.
examples.cn: 没有哪条科学定律禁止这种模式，只是从未有人见过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「赛恩提菲克-罗」——被自然反复遵守的那条规则：科学定律

root: scientific 来自拉丁语 scientia「知识」← scire「知道」；law 来自古诺尔斯语 lag「被放下之物」→ lagu，与拉丁语 lex 无关。「自然规律」的比喻盛行于十七世纪，完整术语在十九世纪定型。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one laid-down regularity: a general statement, a named physical law, the describing half of law and theory, a quantitative law, a conservation law, the philosophical law of nature, a biological regularity, a social tendency and a mathematical law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着一条被立下的稳定性：一般陈述、有专名的物理定律、定律与理论中「描述」的那一半、定量定律、守恒定律、哲学上的自然规律、生物稳定性、社会趋势与数学定律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one short equation on a plaque, surrounded by decades of data tables that all agree with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：牌子上一条简短等式，周围贴满几十年都与它吻合的数据表。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE EQUATION: a regularity stated in words, then in measurable numbers.
branches.cn: 模式与等式：先用文字陈述的稳定性，再用可测数字陈述。

branches.en: THE NAMED AND THE CONSERVED: Newton's laws cited by name, and quantities that cannot be lost.
branches.cn: 具名与守恒：被按名引用的牛顿定律，与不能损失的物理量。

branches.en: THE PARTNER OF THEORY: what happens, set beside why it happens.
branches.cn: 理论的搭档：发生什么，与为何发生并列。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: nature imagined as obeying commands written into matter.
branches.cn: 那个比喻：自然被想象成服从写进物质的命令。

branches.en: THE LOOSER LAWS: ratios in inheritance, tendencies in markets, theorems in mathematics.
branches.cn: 较宽松的定律：遗传中的比例、市场中的趋势、数学中的定理。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Norse-derived noun, and neither half is built from the other.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语来源的形容词与诺尔斯语来源的名词接在一起，两半都不由对方构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer belongs to scientific alone: scire, sciens and scientia. Law is Norse, and lex is a separate Latin line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分只属于 scientific 这一半：scire、sciens 与 scientia。law 来自诺尔斯语，lex 则是另一条拉丁语线。

items.example: The phrase is a modern pairing of two different origins.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语把两个不同来源的词配在一起。

items.example: It supplies the adjective half.
items.exampleCN: 它提供形容词那一半。

items.example: The noun behind scientific.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词背后的名词。

items.example: The adjective means knowledge-making.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词意为「产生知识的」。

items.example: The image is a thing placed in position.
items.exampleCN: 意象是被安置到位的东西。

items.example: English borrowed the plural as law.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入复数形式作「法律」。

items.example: The legal and scientific senses share one image.
items.exampleCN: 法律义与科学义共享一个意象。

items.example: It gives legal and legitimate, not law.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「合法的」与「正当的」二词，而非「法律」。

items.example: The look-alike that belongs to the other line.

definition_zh: 创造力；创造性；独创性；创作能力
definition_en: the ability to produce original ideas, works or solutions
core_image: 三样毫不相干的物件在孩子手里被拼成一个能站住的新东西。
scene: 工作室的墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后留下来的方案把两种旧工具合成了一种新用法。 The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
sceneCN: 这里 creativity 指「产生原创想法或作品的能力」（第 1 个义项：造出此前不存在之物的总体能力）；句意为墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。可辨识物件：草稿墙、旧工具、工作台、最终方案。

pos.zh: 创造力；创造性；独创性

senses.title: The power to make something new
senses.titleCN: 造出新事物的总体能力
senses.definition: the general ability to produce ideas, works or solutions that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 产生此前不存在的观念、作品或解决办法的总体能力
senses.example: The studio's walls were covered with rejected drafts before creativity produced a new use for two old tools.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上贴满被否掉的草稿，最后创造力把两种旧工具合成一种新用法。
senses.why: The noun is built on create, so it names the power behind making something that was not there.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建立在「创造」之上，因此指造出原本不存在之物的能力。

senses.title: The quality of being creative
senses.definition: the degree to which an idea or work shows original invention
senses.definitionCN: 一个观念或作品显示原创发明的程度
senses.example: Judges scored the entries for creativity rather than polish.
senses.exampleCN: 评委按创造性而非完成度给参赛作品打分。
senses.why: The abstract noun can name a measurable quality, which is how competitions and schools use it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象名词可以指一种可测量的性质，比赛与学校正是这样使用它。

senses.title: Originality that stands apart
senses.definition: the quality of being unlike what already exists, especially in a striking way
senses.definitionCN: 与既有之物不同、尤指以显著方式不同的性质
senses.example: The building's creativity lies in what it leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的独创性在于它省略了什么。
senses.why: Newness alone is not enough; the word often implies a difference that others can recognize.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的新还不够；这个词常暗示一种别人能认出的差异。

senses.title: The artist's working power
senses.definition: the capacity to invent and shape works in a medium such as paint, sound or words
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画、声音或文字等媒介中发明并塑造作品的能力
senses.example: Her creativity shows most clearly in small drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 她的创作能力在小幅画作中最清楚。
senses.why: Art gives the power a medium, so creativity becomes the ability to shape material into a new form.
senses.whyCN: 艺术给这种能力一个媒介，于是创造力成为把材料塑成新形式的本领。

senses.title: Creativity shared by a group
senses.definition: the combined ability of a group to generate and develop new ideas
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体产生并发展新观念的综合能力
senses.example: Team creativity improved when the quiet members spoke first.
senses.exampleCN: 当沉默的成员先发言时，团队创造力提高了。
senses.why: Organizations treat creativity as a group resource, so the noun is used for a collective rather than one mind.
senses.whyCN: 组织把创造力当作群体资源，因此这个名词用于集体，而非单个头脑。

senses.title: Creative thinking as a process
senses.titleCN: 作为过程的创造性思维
senses.definition: the process of generating, combining and testing novel ideas
senses.definitionCN: 产生、组合并检验新颖观念的过程
senses.example: Creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
senses.exampleCN: 创造力常常是一个制作与丢弃的循环。
senses.why: The noun can name the activity itself, including its failures, not only the final ability.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指活动本身，包括其中的失败，而不只是最终能力。

senses.title: A period or burst of invention
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which a person or group produces an unusual amount of new work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或群体产出异常多新作品的一段时间
senses.example: The letters record a burst of creativity before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件记录了战前一次创造力的迸发。
senses.why: Creativity is uneven, so the word also names its high periods rather than a steady trait.
senses.whyCN: 创造力并不均匀，因此这个词也指它的高峰期，而非稳定特质。

senses.title: Inventiveness in a field
senses.titleCN: 某一领域中的创造能力
senses.definition: the ability to make original contributions within a particular discipline, such as science or business
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定学科、如科学或商业中作出原创贡献的能力
senses.example: Scientific creativity often looks like a better question, not a louder answer.
senses.exampleCN: 科学创造力常常表现为更好的问题，而不是更响亮的答案。
senses.why: Each field defines what counts as new, so the word takes on the standards of that discipline.
senses.whyCN: 每个领域都定义什么才算新，因此这个词会带上该学科的标准。

intro.en: Creativity is an English noun formed from creative, which comes from create, from Latin creare, to make or bring forth.
intro.cn: creativity 是由 creative 构成的英语名词；creative 来自 create，而 create 来自拉丁 creare「制造、产生」。

items.en: Creare meant to make, bring forth or produce, and was used of gods, parents and makers alike. Its deeper origin is generally considered to involve a reconstructed root, and the exact earlier form is not settled.
items.cn: creare 意为制造、产生或产出，可用于神、父母与制作者。其更早来源一般被认为涉及某个重构词根，确切更早形态尚无定论。

items.en: The action noun creatio named the making, and in Christian writing it became the word for the creation of the world.
items.cn: 动作名词 creatio 指制造行为；在基督教写作中，它成为「创世」一词。

items.en: English create entered in the fifteenth century through French, first in the sense of bringing something into existence.
items.cn: 英语 create 在十五世纪经法语进入，最初指使某物存在。

items.en: Creative added the adjective suffix to create in the seventeenth century; for a long time it described a divine or artistic making.
items.cn: creative 在十七世纪由 create 加形容词后缀而成；很长时间里它描述神圣或艺术的创造。

items.en: Creativity appeared as a noun in the nineteenth century, and psychology made it a measurable subject in the twentieth.
items.cn: creativity 在十九世纪作为名词出现，心理学在二十世纪把它变成可测量的研究对象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first recorded use of creativity and pre-Latin origin of make): the earliest English citation of the noun is not firmly dated, and the deeper source of creare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词首次记录与「制造」义的拉丁语之前来源）：creativity 最早的英语书证没有确切年代；creare 的更早来源属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the making family that are easy to confuse; group two holds near names for inventive power.
note.cn: 第一组是「制造」词族中容易混淆的词；第二组是表示创造能力的近义词。

entries.definition: The act of making something, or the thing made; creativity is the ability behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的动作，或被造之物；creativity 是背后的能力。

entries.definition: A person who makes something; the maker is not the power that the maker uses.
entries.definitionCN: 制造某物的人；制造者并不等于他所运用的能力。

entries.definition: Having the power to create; creativity is the noun for that power.
entries.definitionCN: 具有创造能力的；creativity 是这种能力的名词。

entries.definition: The producing of offspring, from a prefix meaning for or forward plus creare; it is not the same as artistic creativity.
entries.definitionCN: 生育后代，由表示「为了、向前」的前缀加 creare 构成；与艺术创造力不同。

entries.definition: The power to picture what is absent or unreal; creativity puts such pictures into works.
entries.definitionCN: 想象不在场或不真实之物的能力；创造力把这类画面变成作品。

entries.definition: A new method or product, especially one that is put into use; innovation stresses adoption, creativity the making.
entries.definitionCN: 新的方法或产品，尤其指被投入使用的；innovation 强调采用，creativity 强调制造。

entries.definition: The quality of being unlike others; originality is one face of creativity, but creativity also covers usefulness and process.
entries.definitionCN: 与众不同的性质；独创性是创造力的一个面向，但创造力也涵盖实用性与过程。

entries.definition: Something new that has been devised; invention is the product, creativity the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 被设计出的新东西；发明是产物，创造力是能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the make root, the noun chain from create to creativity, and the wall of rejected drafts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「制造」词根、从 create 到 creativity 的名词链，以及贴满被否草稿的墙。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to make or bring forth; the noun chain runs create, creative, creativity.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为制造或产生；名词链依次是 create、creative、creativity。

normal.en: The family runs create, creation, creative, creator, creativity and creatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 create、creation、creative、creator、creativity 与 creatively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: artistic creativity, team creativity, creativity research.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：艺术创造力、团队创造力、创造力研究。

normal.en: The word names a capacity, a quality and a period: a person has it, a work shows it, a year can be one.
normal.cn: 这个词兼指能力、性质与时期：人有它，作品显示它，某一年也可以是它。

normal.en: Rejected drafts are part of the word: creativity is often a loop of making and discarding.
normal.cn: 被否掉的草稿也是这个词的一部分：创造力常常是制作与丢弃的循环。

abstract.en: Picture three unrelated objects lying together until a child joins them into something that stands.
abstract.cn: 想象三件毫不相干的物件躺在一起，直到孩子把它们拼成一个能站住的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of crossed-out drawings with one clean sheet at the end.
abstract.cn: 想象一面画满又被划掉的墙，尽头只剩一张干净的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that becomes a tree no one had planted before.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子长成一棵从前无人种过的树。

examples.en: The workshop was designed to give employees time for creativity.
examples.cn: 这个工作坊的设计是为了给员工留出发挥创造力的时间。

examples.en: Creativity rarely appears on a schedule, but it can be given room.
examples.cn: 创造力很少按日程出现，但可以给它空间。

examples.en: Her creativity turned a broken bicycle into a garden cart.
examples.cn: 她的创造力把一辆坏自行车改成了园艺推车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把没有关系的东西拼成一个站得住的新东西 → 创造力

root: 拉丁 creare「制造、产生」→ 动作名词 creatio → 英语 create；加形容词后缀成 creative，再加抽象名词后缀成 creativity。creare 更早来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one making: something new is brought into being, and the same power is read as a quality, an originality, an artistic skill, a group resource, a process, a burst and a field-specific contribution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次制造展开：新事物被带入存在；同一种能力随后被读作性质、独创性、艺术技艺、群体资源、过程、迸发期以及特定领域的贡献。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three unrelated objects joined into one new thing that can stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：三件毫不相干的物件被拼成一个能站住的新东西。

branches.en: THE POWER AND THE PROCESS: the ability and the loop of making are both named.
branches.cn: 能力与过程：能力本身与制作循环都可用这个词指称。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: a work can be scored for newness and for difference.
branches.cn: 性质：作品可以按新颖度与差异度被打分。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: paint, sound and words give the power a body.
branches.cn: 媒介：绘画、声音与文字给这种能力一个身体。

branches.en: THE GROUP AND THE MOMENT: creativity can belong to a team or to a season.
branches.cn: 群体与时刻：创造力可以属于一个团队，也可以属于一个时期。

branches.en: THE FIELD: each discipline decides what counts as a new contribution.
branches.cn: 领域：每个学科自己决定什么算新的贡献。

intro.en: Creativity is the end of a short Latin chain: a verb of making becomes a noun, an adjective and finally an abstract noun of ability.
intro.cn: creativity 是一条简短拉丁链的末端：制造动词先成名词，再成形容词，最后成为表示能力的抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin creare gives create, creation, creator, creative and creativity; the suffixes -ive and -ity carry the chain forward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 creare 衍生 create、creation、creator、creative 与 creativity；形容词与抽象名词后缀推动这条链向前。

items.example: The team created a new map.
items.exampleCN: 团队创造了一张新地图。

items.meaning: the act of making or the thing made
items.example: The creation took three years.
items.exampleCN: 这件作品的创作花了三年。

items.example: The creator left the ending open.

items.example: The creative team met on Mondays.

items.example: Creativity needs both time and waste.

senses.definition: a person who performs balancing and jumping feats

intro.en: Acrobat comes from Greek akrobatos, 'walking on tiptoe', from akros, 'high or tip', and bainein, 'to walk'.
intro.cn: acrobat 来自希腊语 akrobatos（踮脚行走），由 akros（高处、尖端）与 bainein（行走）构成。

items.en: akros meant 'highest, at the tip'.
items.cn: akros 意为「最高的、尖端的」。

items.en: bainein meant 'to walk, to step'.
items.cn: bainein 意为「行走、迈步」。

items.en: akrobatos meant 'one who walks on tiptoe or on a high edge'.
items.cn: akrobatos 意为「踮脚或在高处行走的人」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the performer's name as acrobata.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入表演者之名，作 acrobata。

items.en: English acrobat named the circus performer.
items.cn: 英语 acrobat 指马戏团表演者。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective and skill nouns; the second gathers other performers and agile people.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词与技艺名词；第二组收其他表演者与灵巧之人。
